subject: body
title: Joints That Bend
about: What a joint is (where two bones meet), the hinge joints at knee and elbow that bend one way like a door, the ball-in-a-cup shoulder and hip that swing in circles, the wrist, ankle, neck and finger joints, the slippery cartilage on bone ends, muscles that pull to bend a joint, which joint works when he kicks, throws or nods, and pads that protect joints. How joints are built is a bridge topic; the moving part is NC PE.1.MS.1.1 and PE.1.MS.1.2 (running, kicking, throwing), PE.1.HF.3.1 (flexibility) and 1.PCH.2.1 (avoiding injury). Read it together and let him bend each joint as it comes up.
tip: Ask him to walk across the room without bending his knees, then with. Which joints did he miss?

cards.q: Your knee and your elbow are joints. What meets at a joint?
cards.note: A joint is the meeting place of two bones. A grown-up has 206 bones, so there are lots of joints to bend.

cards.q: Your knee bends one way and straightens back, like a door swinging. What kind of joint is that?
cards.note: A door hinge opens and shuts one way. So does your knee.

cards.q: Which joint in your arm bends like a door hinge?
cards.note: Bend your elbow and your hand comes up to your face. Straighten it and your arm is long again.

cards.q: Your shoulder lets your arm swing all the way around in a circle. What is it shaped like?
cards.note: The round top of your arm bone sits in a cup on your shoulder. It can roll in any direction.

cards.q: Which joint lets your whole leg swing in a big circle, up at the top of your leg?
cards.note: Your hip is a ball-in-a-cup joint too. Swing your leg forward, sideways and back.

cards.q: You swing your lower leg to kick a ball. Which joint bends?
cards.note: Your hip swings the leg and your knee snaps it straight. Both joints help you kick.

cards.q: You throw a ball far. Which joint swings your whole arm around?
cards.note: A big throw uses the shoulder, then the elbow, then the wrist, all in a row.

cards.q: You nod your head yes. Which part has the joints that move?
cards.note: Small joints in your neck let your head nod yes, shake no and tilt sideways.

cards.q: You wave hello and your hand flaps up and down. Which joint bends?
cards.note: Your wrist bends up and down and tilts side to side. It has lots of little bones inside.

cards.q: You stand on tiptoe to reach a shelf. Which joint bends to lift your heel?
cards.note: Your ankle moves your foot up and down like a hinge. Circle your foot to feel it.

cards.q: How many joints are in one of your fingers?
cards.note: Look at the knuckle, the middle and the tip. Your thumb has two.

cards.q: Which is the biggest joint in your body?
cards.note: The knee joins your thigh bone and your shin bone and carries you all day.

cards.q: Can your knee bend backward the way it bends forward?
cards.note: A hinge only goes one way, and that keeps your knee safe. Never force a joint the wrong way.

cards.q: The ends of bones in a joint are covered with smooth, slippery stuff. What is it called?
cards.note: Say KAR-tih-lij. It lets bones glide instead of grind, and your ears and the tip of your nose are cartilage too.

cards.q: What pulls on your bones to make a joint bend?
cards.note: Muscles only pull, they never push. One muscle bends your elbow and another pulls it straight.

cards.q: Which three moves happen at your joints?
cards.note: Every move you make happens at a joint. Stiff legs with no knees could not run.

cards.q: Knee pads and elbow pads protect which parts when you skate or ride a scooter?
cards.note: A helmet protects the skull. Pads protect the joints that hit the ground first in a fall.
